title.zh: 卷385 列傳一百七十二 杜受田子：翰 祁俊藻子：世长 翁心存 彭蕴章
title.en: Volume 385 Biographies 172: Du Shoutian Son: Han, Qi Junzao Son: Shi Zhang, Weng Xincun, Peng Yunzhang
title.raw: 卷385 列傳一百七十二 杜受田子：翰 祁俊藻子：世长 翁心存 彭蕴章

sentences.zh: 杜受田，字芝農，山東濱州人。

translations.literal: Du Shoutian, courtesy name Zhinong, was a man of Binzhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shoutian, whose courtesy name was Zhinong, came from Binzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父堮，嘉慶六年進士，由翰林院編修累官禮部侍郎，重宴鹿鳴，加太子少保，卒贈太傅，諡文端。

translations.literal: His father Fu was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 受田，道光三年進士，會試第一，殿試二甲第一，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Shoutian passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Daoguang, ranked first in the metropolitan examination and first in the second class of the palace examination, was selected as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shoutian became a jinshi in 1823, topping both the metropolitan and palace examinations (first in the second class), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考擢中允，遷洗馬，督山西學政。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he was promoted to household attendant, transferred to director of instruction, and supervised education in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a palace examination promotion he rose to household attendant and then director of instruction, and was sent to supervise provincial examinations in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特召還京，直上書房，授文宗讀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially summoned back to the capital, entered the Upper Study, and instructed Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was specially recalled to Beijing, assigned to the Upper Study, and charged with tutoring the future Emperor Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 四遷內閣學士，命專心授讀，毋庸到閣批本。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became a Grand Secretariat academician; he was ordered to devote himself solely to instruction and was excused from attending the Grand Secretariat to endorse memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted four times to grand secretariat academician, he was ordered to focus entirely on teaching and was relieved of routine duty endorsing memorials at the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted Vice Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he was made vice minister of works and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，連擢左都御史、工部尚書，尋充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted in succession to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and Minister of Works, and soon thereafter appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 he was promoted in quick succession to left censor-in-chief and minister of works, and soon became chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 文宗自六歲入學，受田朝夕納誨，必以正道，歷十餘年。

translations.literal: Wenzong began study at age six; Shoutian instructed him morning and evening with the proper Way, for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng had begun his lessons at six; for more than a decade Shoutian guided him day and night along the right path.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗晚年，以文宗長且賢，欲付大業，猶未決。

translations.literal: By the late years of Xuanzong, as Wenzong was eldest and virtuous, the emperor wished to entrust him with the great enterprise but had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's last years, though the heir was eldest and clearly capable, the emperor still had not settled on him for the succession.

sentences.zh: 會校獵南苑，諸皇子皆從，恭親王奕訢獲禽最多，文宗未發一矢，問之，對曰：「時方春，鳥獸孳育，不忍傷生以乾天和。」

translations.literal: Once during a hunting review at the Southern Park all the princes followed; Prince Gong Yixin took the most game, while Wenzong had not loosed a single arrow. When asked, he replied: 'It is now spring; birds and beasts are breeding—I cannot bear to harm living things and disturb Heaven's harmony.'
translations.idiomatic: During a hunt in the Southern Park all the princes were present. Prince Gong Yixin bagged the most game, but the prince who would become Xianfeng did not shoot once. Asked why, he answered: 'It is spring; the birds and beasts are breeding. I cannot bear to kill them and offend Heaven's harmony.'

sentences.zh: 宣宗大悅，曰：「此真帝者之言！」

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly pleased and said: 'These are truly the words of an emperor!'
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang was delighted and exclaimed: 'Those are truly a Son of Heaven's words!'

sentences.zh: 立儲遂密定，受田輔導之力也。

translations.literal: The decision to establish the heir was thus settled in secret—the result of Shoutian's guiding influence.
translations.idiomatic: The choice of heir was quietly fixed—owing in large part to Shoutian's tutelage.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，加太子太傅，兼署吏部尚書，調刑部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Wenzong ascended the throne, Shoutian was given Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently served as Minister of Personnel, was transferred to Minister of Justice and appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfeng took the throne in 1850, Shoutian was made grand tutor of the heir apparent, briefly headed the Ministry of Personnel, then the Ministry of Justice, and was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 受田雖未入樞廷，國家大政及進退大臣，上必諮而後行。

translations.literal: Although Shoutian had not entered the Grand Council, on great affairs of state and the appointment or dismissal of high ministers the emperor always consulted him before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Though he never sat on the Grand Council, the emperor consulted him on every major policy and every senior appointment or dismissal before acting.

sentences.zh: 廣西軍事亟，受田數陳方略，薦林則徐、週天爵，先後起用。

translations.literal: The Guangxi military situation was urgent; Shoutian repeatedly presented strategy and recommended Lin Zexu and Zhou Tianjue, who were successively reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: As the Guangxi crisis worsened, he repeatedly outlined strategy and urged the reinstatement of Lin Zexu and Zhou Tianjue, both of whom were eventually recalled to service.

sentences.zh: 提督向榮老於軍事，以同列不和被謗，力陳輿論，數保全之。

translations.literal: The commander Xiang Rong, experienced in warfare, was slandered for not getting along with peers; [Shoutian] forcefully cited public opinion and repeatedly secured his position.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran commander Xiang Rong was attacked for clashing with colleagues; Shoutian cited public opinion and several times kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，調管禮部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to head the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was transferred to head the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年，因河決豐北久未塞，山東、江北被災重，命偕福州將軍怡良往治賑務。

translations.literal: In the second year, because the Yellow River breach at north Feng had long gone unrepaired and Shandong and Jiangbei suffered severe disaster, he was ordered together with Fuzhou General Yiliang to go and oversee relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, with the north Fengzhou breach still open and Shandong and north Jiangsu devastated, he was sent with Fuzhou general Yiliang to supervise relief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「災廣民眾，賑恤不可緩，尤在得人。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'The disaster is widespread and the people numerous; relief cannot be delayed, and selecting the right men is especially important.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'The disaster is vast and the people many—relief must not wait, and above all the right officials must be chosen.'

sentences.zh: 薦山東布政使劉源灝、江寧布政使祁宿藻，皆持正有為，責成專任；

translations.literal: He recommended Shandong provincial treasurer Liu Yuanhao and Jiangning provincial treasurer Qi Suzao, both upright and capable, entrusting them with full responsibility;
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Shandong treasurer Liu Yuanhao and Jiangning treasurer Qi Suzao—both upright and energetic—and gave each sole charge of relief;

sentences.zh: 請截留江、廣漕米六十萬石分給兩省；

translations.literal: he requested that six hundred thousand shi of grain transport from Jiangsu and Guangdong be diverted for distribution to the two provinces;
translations.idiomatic: he asked that six hundred thousand shi of tribute grain from Jiangsu and Guangdong be held back and divided between the two provinces;

sentences.zh: 詔並允行。

translations.literal: the edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved everything.

sentences.zh: 受田自侍文宗學，未嘗離左右，當陛辭，不覺感戀流涕。

translations.literal: Shoutian had attended Wenzong's studies and had never left his side; when taking leave at court he could not help weeping from affection.
translations.idiomatic: Having never left the prince's side since tutoring began, he wept openly when bidding farewell at court.

sentences.zh: 在途觸暑染疫，力疾治事，與源灝、宿藻等覈定施賑章程，疏陳而不言病，至清江浦遽卒。

translations.literal: On the road he caught plague from the heat and pressed on with affairs despite illness; with Yuanhao, Suzao and others he verified and fixed relief regulations, memorializing without mentioning his illness, until he died suddenly at Qingjiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he fell ill in the heat but kept working; with Yuanhao, Suzao, and others he finalized relief rules and memorialized without mentioning his sickness, then died suddenly at Qingjiangpu.

sentences.zh: 遺疏念賊氛未靖，河患未平，尤以敬天法祖、勤政愛民、崇節儉、慎好惡、平賞罰為言。

translations.literal: His final memorial expressed concern that bandit unrest was not pacified and river disaster not settled, and above all urged reverence for Heaven and ancestral law, diligent government and love for the people, esteem for frugality, care in likes and dislikes, and evenhanded rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed memorial still worried that rebels were unbeaten and the river unrestored, and urged above all reverence for Heaven and the ancestors, diligent rule, love for the people, frugality, careful likes and dislikes, and fair rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 文宗震悼，贈太師、大學士，入祀賢良祠，賜金五千兩治喪，遣近臣慰視其父堮，擢其子檢討翰為庶子，孫三人並賜舉人。

translations.literal: Wenzong was deeply grieved; he posthumously granted Grand Tutor and Grand Secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, granted five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close official to comfort his father Fu, promoted his son the compiler Han to chamberlain for the heir, and granted all three grandsons the status of provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng was stricken: he posthumously made Shoutian grand tutor and grand secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, gave five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close minister to console his father Fu, promoted his son Han from reviewer to chamberlain of the heir apparent, and granted all three grandsons the juren degree.

sentences.zh: 复特詔曰：「杜受田品端學粹，正色立朝，皇考深加倚重，特簡為朕師傅。

translations.literal: A special edict said: 'Du Shoutian's character was upright and learning pure; he remonstrated at court with proper bearing. My late father greatly relied on him and specially chose him as my tutor.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict read: "Du Shoutian was upright in conduct and pure in learning, and spoke with moral authority at court. My late father relied on him deeply and chose him especially as my teacher.

sentences.zh: 憶在書齋，凡所陳說，悉本唐、虞、三代聖聖相傳之旨，實能發明蘊奧，體用兼賅。

translations.literal: Recalling the study hall, everything he expounded was based on the transmitted purport of the sage kings from Tang, Yu and the Three Dynasties, truly able to elucidate hidden meaning with principle and application combined.
translations.idiomatic: In the study, everything he taught drew on the succession of sage-kings from Tang and Yu through the Three Dynasties; he could unfold their deepest meaning with both principle and practice intact.

sentences.zh: 朕即位後，週諮時政利弊，民生疾苦，盡心獻替，啟沃良多！

translations.literal: After my accession, whenever I consulted on the pros and cons of policy and the hardships of the people's livelihood, he devoted his mind to counsel, giving much nurturing guidance!
translations.idiomatic: After I came to the throne, whenever I asked about policy and the people's hardships, he gave his whole mind to counsel—guidance I cannot count!

sentences.zh: 援嘉慶朝大學士硃珪故事，特諡文正。」

translations.literal: Following the precedent of Grand Secretary Zhu Gui in the Jiaqing reign, he was specially granted the posthumous title Wen Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Jiaqing precedent of Grand Secretary Zhu Gui, he was given the posthumous name Wen Zheng (Cultured and Upright)."

sentences.zh: 謂其公忠正直，足當「正」字而無愧。

translations.literal: [The edict] said he was so loyal and upright as fully to deserve the character 'zheng' without shame.
translations.idiomatic: The edict held that his public loyalty and integrity fully deserved the word 'upright' without qualification.

sentences.zh: 柩至京，上親奠，撫棺哭甚哀，晉其父堮禮部尚書銜。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor personally offered sacrifice, caressed the coffin and wept bitterly, and promoted his father Fu with the nominal rank of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached Beijing the emperor sacrificed in person, stroked the bier, and wept bitterly, and raised his father Fu with the honorary rank of minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，上臨雍講學，复詔褒受田曩日講貫之功，即家賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: The next year when the emperor lectured at the imperial school, he again issued an edict praising Shoutian's past instruction and granted a sacrificial altar at his home.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the imperial lecture at the National University, he again praised Shoutian's teaching and granted a sacrificial altar at his home.

sentences.zh: 及柩歸，命恭親王奠送，遣官到籍致祭，飾終之典，一時無與比。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, Prince Gong was ordered to escort it with sacrifices; officials were sent to his native place for rites—the funeral honors were unmatched at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin went home, Prince Gong was ordered to escort it; officials were sent to his native place for rites—funeral honors unequaled in the age.

sentences.zh: 子，由翰林院編修累官戶部侍郎，督辦山東團練。

translations.literal: [His] son [Han], rising from Hanlin compiler to Vice Minister of Revenue, supervised Shandong militia training.
translations.idiomatic: His son, rising from Hanlin compiler to vice minister of revenue, supervised militia training in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 翰，字繼園。

translations.literal: Han, courtesy name Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han, courtesy name Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, selected bachelor, appointed reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1844, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was made a reviewer.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補庶子。

translations.literal: After mourning, restored as chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was restored as chamberlain of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文宗念受田舊勞，數月間迭擢工部侍郎，命在軍機大臣上行走，辦理京城巡防事宜。

translations.literal: Wenzong mindful of Shoutian's old service, within months promoted him repeatedly to Vice Minister of Works and ordered him to serve above the Grand Council ministers managing capital patrol defense.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Shoutian's service, Xianfeng within months raised him repeatedly to vice minister of works and ordered him to serve above the Grand Councilors in charge of capital defense.

sentences.zh: 翰勇於任事，甚被倚任。

translations.literal: Han was bold in undertaking affairs and greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Han was bold in action and deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 十年，隨扈熱河，以勞賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, accompanying the emperor to Rehe, rewarded with the peacock feather for labor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he followed the court to Rehe and was rewarded with the peacock feather for his exertions.

sentences.zh: 上崩於行在，穆宗即位。

translations.literal: The emperor died at the traveling palace; Muzong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died at the traveling palace and Tongzhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 御史董元醇疏請兩宮皇太后垂簾聽政，載垣、端華、肅順等持不可，翰附之，抗言甚力，遂黜元醇議。

translations.literal: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized asking the two empress dowagers to attend court behind the curtain; Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun and others objected; Han sided with them and argued forcefully, so Dong's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Yuanchun asked that the two empress dowagers rule from behind a screen; Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and their party objected; Han sided with them and argued fiercely, and Dong's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 肅順曰：「君誠不愧杜文正之子也！」

translations.literal: Sushun said: 'Sir, you are truly worthy of being Du Wen Zheng's son!'
translations.idiomatic: Sushun said: 'You are indeed worthy of Du Wen Zheng's son!'

sentences.zh: 既而載垣等以竊奪政柄被罪，翰連坐，議革職戍新疆，詔原之，褫職，免其發遣。

translations.literal: Soon Zaiyuan and others were condemned for seizing power; Han was implicated, was to be dismissed and banished to Xinjiang; an edict pardoned him—stripped of office but exempted from exile.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaiyuan and the others fell for usurping power, Han was implicated and sentenced to dismissal and banishment to Xinjiang; an edict pardoned him—he lost office but was spared exile.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1866.

sentences.zh: 祁俊藻，字春圃，山西壽陽人。

translations.literal: Qi Junzao, courtesy name Chunpu, was a man of Shouyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Junzao, whose courtesy name was Chunpu, came from Shouyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父韻士，官戶部郎中，以事繫獄。

translations.literal: His father Yunshi was a director in the Ministry of Revenue and was imprisoned for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunshi was a director in the Ministry of Revenue and was jailed over a case.

sentences.zh: 俊藻方幼，隨侍讀書不輟，賦春草詩以見志。

translations.literal: Junzao was still young; he followed his father in study without pause and composed a poem on spring grass to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Still a boy, he kept reading at his father's side and wrote a poem on spring grass to show his intent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1814, entered the Hanlin, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 督湖南學政，累遷庶子。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Hunan and was promoted in succession to chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised Hunan examinations and rose to chamberlain of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，以母病陳情歸養，宣宗不許，予假省親。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, citing his mother's illness he asked to return home to care for her; Xuanzong did not permit it but granted leave to visit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1830, pleading his mother's illness, he asked to go home; Daoguang refused a full retirement but granted leave to visit.

sentences.zh: 逾年回京，補原官，遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned to the capital, resumed his former post, and was promoted reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned, resumed his post, and was made reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋复予假省母，不開缺。

translations.literal: Soon he was again granted leave to visit his mother without vacating his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given leave again to see his mother, without losing his rank.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司副使、光祿寺卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，十六年，將屆服闋，預授兵部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home; in the sixteenth year, as his mourning was about to end, he was appointed in advance Vice Minister of War and supervisor of education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, in 1836, just before mourning ended, he was named in advance vice minister of war and Jiangsu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部侍郎，留學政任，未滿，十九年，命偕侍郎黃爵滋視福建海防及禁煙事，連擢左都御史、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue and of Personnel, retained the education commission before its term ended, and in the nineteenth year was ordered together with Vice Minister Huang Juezi to inspect Fujian coastal defense and the opium ban; he was promoted in succession to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice minister of revenue and of personnel, kept the education post, and in 1839 was sent with Huang Juezi to inspect Fujian's coast and opium suppression, then promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 迭疏陳總宜駐泉州治防務，改海口砲台為墩，查禁煙販，捕治漢奸，並禁漳、泉兩府行使夷錢，夾帶私鑄者治罪，嚴懲械鬥，並得旨允行。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly that headquarters should be at Quanzhou for defense, that coastal batteries should be converted to blockhouses, that opium trafficking should be banned, Han traitors punished, foreign coins forbidden in Zhang and Quan prefectures with private minting punished, and armed brawls severely punished—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials he urged basing defense at Quanzhou, turning seacoast batteries into blockhouses, banning opium, punishing collaborators, forbidding foreign coin in Zhang and Quan, punishing private minting, and cracking down on feuds—all approved.

sentences.zh: 在閩半載，還經浙江，按台、溫兩府私種罌粟，劾罷台州知府潘盛；

translations.literal: After half a year in Fujian, returning by way of Zhejiang he investigated private poppy cultivation in Tai and Wen prefectures and impeached Taizhou prefect Pan Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: After six months in Fujian he passed through Zhejiang, found illicit poppy in Taizhou and Wenzhou, and impeached Taizhou prefect Pan Sheng;

sentences.zh: 又劾溫州知府劉煜試行票鹽不善，被議，自呈枉屈，戍新疆。

translations.literal: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for mishandling the ticket-salt trial and was himself censured; he submitted that he had been wronged and was banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for botching a ticket-salt trial, was himself censured, protested injustice, and was sent to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 時鄧廷楨奏擊英吉利兵船於廈門走之，忌者謂其不實，命俊藻復往按，具陳戰胜狀。

translations.literal: At that time Deng Tingzhen memorialized that he had driven off British warships at Xiamen; jealous parties said this was untrue, and Junzao was sent again to investigate and fully reported the victory.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Tingzhen reported driving British ships from Xiamen, rivals called it false; Junzao was sent to verify and confirmed the victory in full.

sentences.zh: 回京，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he again served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he again served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調戶部，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he moved to the Ministry of Revenue and joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕尚書文慶按長蘆鹽運使陳鑑挪撥鹽課，彌補加價，褫其職，歷任鹽政運司議譴有差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Minister Wen Qing he investigated Changlu salt transport commissioner Chen Jian's diversion of salt revenue to cover price increases; Chen was dismissed and successive salt officials were censured to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846, with Wen Qing, he investigated Changlu transport commissioner Chen Jian for diverting salt revenue to cover surcharges; Chen was dismissed and past salt officials punished in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士，命赴甘肅偕琦善按前任總督布彥泰清查舛誤、縱容家丁，下嚴議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary, he was ordered to Gansu with Qi Shan to investigate former governor-general Buyantai for errors in accounts and indulgence of household servants; severe punishment was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849, as revenue minister and associate grand secretary, he went to Gansu with Qi Shan to investigate ex-governor-general Buyantai for accounting errors and tolerating servants; Buyantai was severely punished.

sentences.zh: 回京，請便道省墓，途次聞宣宗崩，過里門不入。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he asked to visit his family's graves en route; on the road he heard of Xuanzong's death and did not enter his home though he passed the gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he asked to visit his ancestors' graves; hearing of Daoguang's death on the road, he passed his own gate without entering.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，拜體仁閣大學士，仍管戶部。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Junzao was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall and still headed the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfeng succeeded, Junzao became grand secretary of the Tiren Hall and still headed revenue.

sentences.zh: 俊藻自道光中論洋務與穆彰阿不合，至是文宗銳意圖治，罷穆彰阿，俊藻遂領樞務，開言路，起用舊臣，俊藻左右之。

translations.literal: Junzao had disagreed with Mujangga on foreign affairs since the Daoguang era; now Wenzong was eager to reform, dismissed Mujangga, and Junzao took the lead in council affairs, opened channels for memorials, and reemployed old ministers—with Junzao guiding him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Daoguang he had clashed with Mujangga over foreign policy; now Xianfeng meant to govern vigorously, removed Mujangga, and Junzao led the council, reopened memorial channels, and brought back veteran ministers—Junzao at his side throughout.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，調管工部，兼管戶部三庫事務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to head the Ministry of Works and also managed the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he headed works and also oversaw the revenue ministry's three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 二年，復調戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he returned to head revenue.

sentences.zh: 廣西匪日熾，出湖南，遂不可製，湖北、江南數省先後淪陷。

translations.literal: Guangxi bandits grew daily fiercer, broke into Hunan, and could no longer be contained; Hubei, Jiangnan, and several other provinces fell in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi rebels grew bolder, poured into Hunan, and slipped beyond control; Hubei, Jiangnan, and province after province fell.

sentences.zh: 軍興財匱，議者試行鈔法，又鑄當百、當五百大錢，皆行之未久而滋弊。

translations.literal: War raised costs and funds ran short; some proposed paper money, and large coins worth a hundred and five hundred cash were also cast—all were tried briefly and soon bred abuse.
translations.idiomatic: War emptied the treasury; reformers tried paper notes and coins worth a hundred and five hundred cash—all failed quickly and bred corruption.

sentences.zh: 尚書肅順同掌戶部事，尚苛刻。

translations.literal: Minister Sushun jointly managed revenue affairs and was harsh in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Sushun shared revenue duties and was notoriously harsh.

sentences.zh: 又湘軍初起，肅順力言其可用，上鄉之，俊藻皆意與齟《齒吾》，屢稱病請罷，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: When the Hunan Army was first raised, Sushun strongly argued it could be used; the emperor favored the idea, but Junzao was at odds with him on all these matters, repeatedly pleaded illness to resign, and received warm edicts urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan's Hunan Army was new, Sushun urged employing it and the emperor agreed; Junzao disagreed on every front, often pleaded illness to quit, and was warmly urged to remain.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，复堅以為請，乃允致仕。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he again insisted firmly on retiring and was permitted to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1854 he insisted again and was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍犯天津，車駕將幸熱河，俊藻密疏切諫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allies attacked Tianjin; the imperial carriage was about to go to Rehe, and Junzao sent a secret memorial urgently remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, as Anglo-French forces threatened Tianjin and the court prepared to flee to Rehe, Junzao sent a secret, urgent remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 又言關中形勝可建都，釐捐病民，北省尤宜急停，並報聞。

translations.literal: He also said the strategic strength of the Guanzhong region could support a capital, that the lijin levy harmed the people and should be halted especially in the north, and reported all this.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Guanzhong's terrain could anchor a capital, that the lijin tax oppressed the people and should stop at once in the north, and sent these views in.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，特詔起用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Muzong ascended the throne and a special edict recalled him to service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Tongzhi succeeded and a special edict called Junzao back to office.

sentences.zh: 疏陳時政六事：曰保護聖躬以崇帝學；

translations.literal: He memorialized on six matters of current policy: to protect the sacred person and exalt imperial learning;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized six reforms: protect the boy emperor and honor his schooling;

sentences.zh: 曰綏輯民心以清盜源；

translations.literal: to soothe the people's hearts and clear the source of banditry;
translations.idiomatic: pacify the people to dry up rebellion at its source;

sentences.zh: 曰重守令以固民心；

translations.literal: to value prefects and magistrates to secure the people's hearts;
translations.idiomatic: hold prefects and magistrates accountable to keep the people loyal;

sentences.zh: 曰開制科以收人才；

translations.literal: to open special examinations to gather talent;
translations.idiomatic: revive special examinations to gather talent;

sentences.zh: 曰速剿山東、河南賊匪，嚴防山西、陝西要隘，以衛畿輔；

translations.literal: to speedily suppress bandits in Shandong and Henan and strictly guard the passes of Shanxi and Shaanxi to protect the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: crush Shandong and Henan rebels quickly and fortify Shanxi and Shaanxi passes to shield the capital;

sentences.zh: 曰敦崇節儉以培元氣。

translations.literal: to promote frugality and nourish the fundamental vitality of the state.
translations.idiomatic: and practice frugality to restore the dynasty's vital energy.

sentences.zh: 言甚切摯，並被嘉納，次第施行。

translations.literal: His words were very earnest and all were praised and adopted and carried out in order.
translations.idiomatic: His language was passionate; the throne praised it, adopted each point, and implemented them in turn.

sentences.zh: 命以大學士銜授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was ordered to receive the rank of Grand Secretary and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was given grand secretary rank and made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，穆宗入學，命直弘德殿，偕翁心存、倭仁、李鴻藻同授讀，摘錄經史二帙進呈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Muzong began study, he was ordered to serve in the Hongde Hall, together with Weng Xincun, Woren, and Li Hongzao to instruct, and excerpts from the classics and histories in two volumes were presented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Tongzhi began lessons, Junzao joined Weng Xincun, Woren, and Li Hongzao in the Hongde Hall, presenting two volumes of excerpts from the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 上讀大學畢，俊藻具疏推陳為人君止於仁之義，略曰：「大學一書，皇上已成誦，凡制治保邦之道，用人行政之源，胥在於是。

translations.literal: When the emperor finished reading the Great Learning, Junzao submitted a memorial elaborating the meaning that the way of the ruler stops at benevolence, in part saying: 'The Great Learning Your Majesty has now mastered—in it lie the ways to order the realm and secure the state, and the sources of employing men and governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi finished the Great Learning, Junzao memorialized on the ruler's duty to stop at benevolence, writing in part: 'Your Majesty has now mastered the Great Learning; in it are the ways to govern and secure the realm and the roots of appointing officials and conducting policy.

sentences.zh: 為人君之道，止於仁而已。

translations.literal: The way of the ruler is simply to stop at benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: For a ruler, the way ends in benevolence alone.

sentences.zh: 治國平天下兩章，言仁者六，終之以未有上好仁而下不好義。

translations.literal: The chapters on bringing order to the state and pacifying all under Heaven mention benevolence six times, ending with the statement that never yet has one above loved benevolence while those below did not love righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The chapters on ordering the state and pacifying the realm speak of benevolence six times, ending with: never yet has a superior loved benevolence while inferiors did not love righteousness.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁者必以仁親為寶，故能愛人，能惡人。

translations.literal: For the benevolent must take benevolence toward kin as treasure and therefore can love men and hate men [properly].
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent take loving kin as their treasure and so can love the worthy and hate the wicked.

sentences.zh: 不好仁，則好人之所惡，惡人之所好。

translations.literal: If one does not love benevolence, one loves what good men hate and hates what good men love.
translations.idiomatic: Without benevolence one loves what the good hate and hates what the good love.

sentences.zh: 仁者必以貪為戒，故忠信以得之，不仁者則驕泰以失之矣。

translations.literal: The benevolent must take greed as a warning; therefore through loyalty and trust they gain it, while the unbenevolent through pride and excess lose it.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent shun greed and gain the realm through loyalty and trust; the unbenevolent lose it through arrogance and excess.

sentences.zh: 仁者以義為利，不以利為利，故以財發身，不仁者則以身發財，菑害並至矣。

translations.literal: The benevolent take righteousness as profit, not profit as profit; therefore they enrich the person with wealth, while the unbenevolent enrich wealth with the person and calamity and harm arrive together.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent take righteousness as profit, not profit as profit; they use wealth to nurture life, while the unbenevolent use life to pile up wealth—and ruin follows together.

sentences.zh: 千古治亂之機，判於義利，而義利之判，則由於上之好仁不好仁也。

translations.literal: The hinge of order and chaos through the ages is decided by righteousness and profit, and the decision between righteousness and profit depends on whether those above love benevolence or do not love benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Through the ages order and chaos turn on the choice between righteousness and profit—and that choice turns on whether the ruler loves benevolence.

sentences.zh: 如近日所講帝鑑圖說，下車泣罪，解網施恩，澤及枯骨等事，斯即帝王仁心所見端也。

translations.literal: As in recent lessons from the Mirror of Emperors—descending from the carriage to weep over crime, loosening the net to show mercy, and grace reaching even dry bones—these are the first signs of an imperial benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: As in your recent lessons from the Mirror of Emperors—stepping down to weep over a criminal, opening the net in mercy, grace even to dry bones—these are the first marks of a ruler's benevolent heart.

sentences.zh: 若納諫求賢，尊儒遠佞，則仁親為寶，能好能惡之說也。

translations.literal: To accept remonstrance and seek the worthy, honor Confucian learning and keep flatterers at a distance—that is the teaching that benevolence toward kin is treasure and one can love and hate aright.
translations.idiomatic: To heed remonstrance, seek worthies, honor the ru and banish sycophants—that is what the text means by taking benevolent kinship as treasure and loving and hating rightly.

sentences.zh: 露台罷工，裘馬卻獻，則以義為利，不以利為利之說也。

translations.literal: Halting work on the terrace stage, declining gifts of fur and horses—that is the teaching of taking righteousness as profit, not profit as profit.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping the terrace project and refusing gifts of fine furs and horses—that illustrates taking righteousness as profit rather than profit as profit.

sentences.zh: 帝鑑圖說講畢，請進講輿地，以會典諸圖簡明，易於指畫。

translations.literal: When lectures on the Mirror of Emperors were finished, he asked to proceed with geography, since the diagrams in the Collected Statutes are concise and easy to point to on a map.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mirror of Emperors was complete, he asked to teach geography, using the clear maps in the Collected Statutes for easy illustration.

sentences.zh: 又耕織圖及內府石刻宋馬遠豳風圖為農桑衣食之原，皇上讀書之暇，隨時講求，庶知稼穡之艱難，懍守成之不易也。」

translations.literal: He also [urged] the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving and the palace rubbing of Ma Yuan's Bin Feng from the Song, as the source of farming, sericulture, clothing and food; in His Majesty's leisure from reading, to study them at all times, so that he might know the hardship of tillage and revere how hard it is to preserve an inheritance.'
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving and the palace copy of Song Ma Yuan's Bin Feng—sources of grain, silk, clothing, and food—so that in spare moments from reading the emperor might study them, learn how hard farming is, and respect how difficult it is to keep a dynasty intact.'

sentences.zh: 二年，上服除，俊藻偕倭仁、李鴻藻上疏曰：「皇上沖齡踐阼，智慧漸開。

translations.literal: In the second year, when mourning ended, Junzao together with Woren and Li Hongzao memorialized, saying: 'Your Majesty ascended the throne in tender years and your wisdom is gradually opening.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863, when mourning ended, Junzao joined Woren and Li Hongzao in a memorial: "Your Majesty took the throne very young and your mind is opening.

sentences.zh: 當此釋服之初，吉禮舉行，聖心之敬肆於此分，風會之轉移即於此始，則玩好之漸可慮也，遊觀之漸可慮也，興作之漸可慮也。

translations.literal: At this beginning of leaving mourning, when auspicious rites are performed, the sacred mind's reverence and relaxation divide here, and the turn of custom begins here—then gradual indulgence in curios may be feared, gradual sightseeing may be feared, gradual construction may be feared.
translations.idiomatic: At this first moment after mourning, when ceremonial rites resume, reverence and ease part ways and custom begins to shift—then one must fear creeping love of trinkets, creeping travel for pleasure, creeping building projects.

sentences.zh: 嗜好之端一開，不惟分誦讀之心，海內之窺意旨者，且將從風而靡。

translations.literal: Once the opening of indulgence is made, it will not only divide the heart for recitation and study; those throughout the realm who watch for the imperial intent will also follow the wind and fall into excess.
translations.idiomatic: Once a taste for luxury opens, it will not only distract from study; everyone watching the court will follow suit.

sentences.zh: 安危治亂之機，其端甚微，所關甚鉅，可無慎乎？

translations.literal: The hinge of safety and danger, order and chaos, begins in something very small yet concerns matters very great—can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: The pivot of order and chaos starts in something tiny yet bears on everything—how can one not be careful?

sentences.zh: 方今軍務未平，生民塗炭，正君臣交儆之時，非上下恬熙之日。

translations.literal: Now military affairs are not yet settled and the people are in misery; this is a time for ruler and ministers to warn each other, not a day for ease above and below.
translations.idiomatic: War is unfinished and the people suffer; this is a time for ruler and ministers to warn each other, not to relax.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇上恪遵慈訓，時時以憂勤惕厲為心，以逸樂便安為戒。

translations.literal: We humbly pray Your Majesty will reverently follow the empress dowagers' instruction, always taking anxious diligence and vigilance to heart and taking ease and comfort as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to heed the empress dowagers' teaching, keep anxious diligence always in mind, and treat comfort as a warning.

sentences.zh: 凡內廷服禦一切用項，稍涉浮靡，概從裁減；

translations.literal: For all inner-court clothing and supplies, whatever is slightly extravagant should in general be cut;
translations.idiomatic: Every inner-court expense that smacks of luxury should be cut;

sentences.zh: 向例所有，不妨量為撙節。

translations.literal: what has been customary may appropriately be reduced in measure.
translations.idiomatic: and long-standing customs may be trimmed where possible.

sentences.zh: 如是，則外務之紛華不接於耳目，詩書之啟迪益斂夫心思，聖學日新，聖德日固，而去奢崇儉之風，自不令而行矣。」

translations.literal: If so, then the gaudy distractions of the outer world will not reach eyes and ears, the enlightenment of poetry and books will further gather the mind, sacred learning will daily renew and sacred virtue daily strengthen, and the wind of rejecting luxury and honoring frugality will prevail without being commanded.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the world's glitter will not reach his eyes and ears, the classics will hold his mind more firmly, learning and virtue will strengthen daily, and frugality will prevail without needing to be ordered."

sentences.zh: 疏上，優詔褒答焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict praised and answered it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up and received a warm, praising reply.

sentences.zh: 俊藻提倡樸學，延納寒素，士林歸之。

translations.literal: Junzao promoted plain learning and welcomed men of humble means; the scholarly world rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Junzao championed solid scholarship and welcomed poor scholars; the literati flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「通經之學，義理與訓詁不可偏重。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'In learning that masters the classics, principle and philology must not be overweighted one against the other.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Classical learning requires both moral principle and textual exegesis—neither may be overweighted.

sentences.zh: 後學不察，以訓詁專屬漢儒，義理專屬宋儒，使畫分界限，學術日歧。」

translations.literal: Later students do not perceive this, assigning philology solely to Han scholars and principle solely to Song scholars, drawing boundaries so that learning daily diverges.'
translations.idiomatic: Later students wrongly assign exegesis to Han learning alone and principle to Song learning alone, drawing lines until scholarship splits."

sentences.zh: 因舉素所知寒士端木埰、鄭珍、莫友芝、閻汝弼、王軒、楊寶臣，經明行修，堪資器使。

translations.literal: He then named poor scholars he had long known—Duanmu Cai, Zheng Zhen, Mo Youzhi, Yan Rubi, Wang Xuan, and Yang Baochen—all versed in the classics and upright in conduct, fit for employment.
translations.idiomatic: He named poor scholars he knew—Duanmu Cai, Zheng Zhen, Mo Youzhi, Yan Rubi, Wang Xuan, and Yang Baochen—learned and upright, fit for office.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「軍興以來，不講吏治，請下中外大臣，保舉循吏及伏處潛修之士，以備任用。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: 'Since the war began, official governance has been neglected; we ask that ministers at court and in the provinces recommend honest local officials and scholars in hidden retirement for appointment.'
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Since the war began, official governance has been neglected; we ask that ministers at court and in the provinces recommend honest local officials and scholars in hidden retirement for appointment."

sentences.zh: 自舉原任同知劉大紳、按察使李文耕、大順廣道劉煦，請宣付史館入循吏傳。

translations.literal: He himself named former subprefect Liu Dashen, surveillance commissioner Li Wengeng, and circuit intendant Liu Xu of Da-Shun-Guang, asking that they be sent to the historiographers for the Biographies of Honest Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Liu Dashen, Li Wengeng, and Liu Xu for the Biographies of Honest Officials.

sentences.zh: 又薦直隸知縣張光藻、陳崇砥、王蘭廣，山東知縣蔣慶第，山西知縣程豫、吳輝祖及江南優貢端木埰，山西舉人秦東來。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zhili magistrates Zhang Guangzao, Chen Chongdi, and Wang Languang; Shandong magistrate Jiang Qingdi; Shanxi magistrates Cheng Yu and Wu Huizu; Jiangnan distinguished graduate Duanmu Cai; and Shanxi provincial graduate Qin Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended magistrates Zhang Guangzao, Chen Chongdi, Wang Languang, Jiang Qingdi, Cheng Yu, and Wu Huizu, plus Duanmu Cai and Qin Donglai.

sentences.zh: 並嘉納允行。

translations.literal: All were praised and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all.

sentences.zh: 屢以病乞休，三年，詔致仕，食全俸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged to retire on grounds of illness; in the third year an edict permitted retirement with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: Illness made him beg retirement repeatedly; in 1864 he was allowed to retire on full pay.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，晉贈太保，祀賢良祠，命鍾郡王奠醊，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; he was posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, Prince Zhong ordered to offer libations, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1866, was posthumously made grand guardian, enshrined among worthies, with Prince Zhong offering libations, and named Wenduan posthumously.

sentences.zh: 擢其子編修世長以侍讀用。

translations.literal: His son the compiler Shizhang was promoted for use as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhang, a compiler, was appointed reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 世長，字子禾。

translations.literal: Shizhang, courtesy name Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang, courtesy name Zihe.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the tenth year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1860.

sentences.zh: 年十三，侍父江蘇學政任，幕客俞正燮、張穆、苗夔諸人，並樸學通儒，世長濡染有素，尤篤守宋儒義理之說。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he attended his father's Jiangsu education commission; staff members Yu Zhengxie, Zhang Mu, Miao Kui and others were all plain-learning masters, and Shizhang was steeped from youth, especially holding fast to Song Neo-Confucian principle.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he followed his father's Jiangsu education post; Yu Zhengxie, Zhang Mu, Miao Kui, and other plain-learning masters were on staff, and Shizhang grew up among them, devoted to Song moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 同治九年，服闋，補侍讀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tongzhi, when mourning ended, he was restored as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870, after mourning, he resumed as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，連督安徽、順天、浙江學政，清勤愛士，一守俊藻舊規。

translations.literal: In the early Guangxu era he supervised examinations in Anhui, Shuntian, and Zhejiang in succession, diligent and loving toward students, holding entirely to Junzao's old rules.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he supervised examinations in Anhui, Shuntian, and Zhejiang, working hard for students and keeping Junzao's standards.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部、吏部侍郎，擢​​左都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Rites and of Personnel and was promoted Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice minister of rites and personnel, then left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十年，命偕尚書延煦勘山東河工，疏言：「非疏海口不能洩盛漲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered together with Minister Yanchi to investigate Shandong river works, memorializing: 'Without dredging the sea mouth the great flood cannot be discharged.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he and Minister Yanchi inspected Shandong river works and wrote: "Without opening the sea mouth the flood cannot be released.

sentences.zh: 修防以民埝為第一層屏障，守民埝即以守大堤。

translations.literal: For repairs and defense the people's embankments are the first layer of barrier; guarding the people's embankments is guarding the great dike.
translations.idiomatic: Repairs should treat folk levees as the first barrier—guarding folk levees guards the main dike.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳士傑築修民埝多在大堤既決之後，殊為失計。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Shijie built and repaired folk embankments mostly after the great dike had already burst—this was greatly mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Shijie rebuilt folk levees mostly after the main dike had already broken—a serious mistake.

sentences.zh: 請乘時興修。」

translations.literal: We ask that repairs be undertaken while the time is right.'
translations.idiomatic: We urge timely repairs."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 迭疏陳時務，多持正議。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly on current affairs, mostly holding to upright views.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized often on public affairs, usually with upright views.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷工部尚書，兼管順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Works and also managed the Shuntian governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1890 he became minister of works and also governed Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 兩典會試，皆得士。

translations.literal: He presided twice over the metropolitan examination and both times obtained good scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he ran the metropolitan exams and both times chose strong graduates.

sentences.zh: 世長清操自勵，累世官卿貳，家如寒素，時以稱焉。

translations.literal: Shizhang disciplined himself with pure conduct; though for generations his family had held high office, the household was like that of the poor—a fact men praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang lived plainly; though his family had held high office for generations, they lived like poor scholars, to everyone's praise.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，優詔賜卹，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died; a gracious edict granted condolence payments and the posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1892 with imperial condolence and the posthumous name Wenke.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫師曾員外郎，子友蒙主事。

translations.literal: His grandson Shizeng was granted secretary in the outer office; his son You was granted secretary in the inner office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shizeng was made an outer-office secretary; his son You an inner-office secretary.

sentences.zh: 翁心存，字二銘，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Weng Xincun, courtesy name Erming, was a man of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Xincun, courtesy name Erming, came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父咸封，官海州學正。

translations.literal: His father Xianfeng was director of studies at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianfeng was Haizhou director of studies.

sentences.zh: 知州唐仲冕見心存有異才，奇之，授之學。

translations.literal: Prefect Tang Zhongmian saw that Xincun had unusual talent, marveled at him, and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tang Zhongmian saw unusual talent in him, took him in, and taught him.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1822, entered the Hanlin, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考擢中允，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he was promoted household attendant and supervised education in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After a palace examination promotion he supervised Guangdong examinations.

sentences.zh: 任滿，入直上書房，授惠郡王讀。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered the Upper Study and instructed Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he joined the Upper Study and tutored Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 尋督江西學政，累遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised education in Jiangxi and was promoted in succession to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He soon supervised Jiangxi examinations and rose to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十七年，复直上書房，授六阿哥讀。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again entered the Upper Study and instructed the Sixth Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he returned to the Upper Study to tutor the sixth prince.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以母老乞養。

translations.literal: After more than a year he asked to retire home to care for his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked leave to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，終母喪。

translations.literal: He remained at home ten years and completed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed home ten years and completed his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 會子同書督貴州學政，陛辭，宣宗命傳諭促之來。

translations.literal: When his son Tongshu was supervising Guizhou education and took leave at court, Xuanzong ordered a message urging him to come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Tongshu left for Guizhou as education commissioner, Daoguang sent word urging Xincun to return.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，至京，仍入直，授八阿哥讀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he reached the capital, again entered regular duty, and instructed the Eighth Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he reached Beijing, resumed duty, and tutored the eighth prince.

sentences.zh: 補祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was made libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 歷內閣學士、工部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Grand Secretariat academician, Vice Minister of Works, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through grand secretariat academician, vice minister of works, and revenue.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫請蘇州、松江、太倉漕米改徵折色，心存謂：「三屬額徵米一百十四萬餘石，一旦改折，慮京倉不敷支放，州縣假折色抑勒倍徵，便民適以累民。」

translations.literal: The Jiangsu governor asked that tribute rice from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang be collected in cash instead; Xincun said: 'The three districts' quota is more than 1,140,000 shi of rice; to change at once to cash collection fears the capital granaries will not have enough for disbursement, and prefectures and counties will use cash collection to extort double levies—convenience for the people will in fact burden the people.'
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangsu asked to collect Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang tribute rice in cash, Xincun said: "The three districts' quota is more than 1.14 million shi of rice; to change at once to cash collection fears the capital granaries will not have enough for disbursement, and prefectures and counties will use cash collection to extort double levies—convenience for the people will in fact burden the people."

sentences.zh: 主駁議，事乃寢。

translations.literal: He led the opposition and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He led opposition and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧陷，心存疏陳兵事，請乘賊勢未定，飭向榮渡江，陳金綬進屯浦口，以上海水師溯流沖其前，江忠源、鄧紹良之師掩其後，四路進攻；

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangning fell, Xincun memorialized on military affairs, asking that while rebel strength was not yet settled, Xiang Rong be ordered to cross the river, Chen Jinshou advance and encamp at Pukou, Shanghai naval forces strike upstream at their front, and the armies of Jiang Zhongyuan and Deng Shaoliang fall on their rear—a four-pronged attack;
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, after Nanjing fell, he urged striking before the rebels settled: Xiang Rong across the Yangzi, Chen Jinshou at Pukou, Shanghai ships upstream, Jiang Zhongyuan and Deng Shaoliang from behind—a four-way assault;

sentences.zh: 增重兵守江、淮杜北竄；

translations.literal: increase heavy forces to guard the Yangzi and Huai to block northward flight;
translations.idiomatic: mass troops on the Yangzi and Huai to block a northward breakout;

sentences.zh: 急清兗、豫、鳳、潁捻匪，毋令與粵寇合勢；

translations.literal: urgently clear Nian bandits in Yan, Yu, Feng, and Ying, and not let them join forces with the Guangdong rebels;
translations.idiomatic: crush Nian bandits in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Henan before they joined the Taiping;

sentences.zh: 並覈軍需，卹災黎；

translations.literal: and verify military supplies and relieve the disaster-stricken populace;
translations.idiomatic: audit supplies and relieve the suffering;

sentences.zh: 籌京倉積貯，整飭紀綱，以維根本。

translations.literal: prepare capital granary stores, rectify discipline, to preserve the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: stock the capital granaries, restore discipline, and secure the dynasty's base.

sentences.zh: 疏上，多被採用。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the memorial was adopted.

sentences.zh: 又薦湖北按察使江忠源，請畀統帥重任，尋即擢為巡撫。

translations.literal: He also recommended Hubei surveillance commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan and asked that heavy command be entrusted to him; soon he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Jiang Zhongyuan for high command; he was soon made governor.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，再調工部，兼管順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Justice, then again to Works, and also managed the Shuntian governor.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to justice, then works again, and also governed Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 粵匪北犯，心存疏言賊氛逼近，請扼河而守，畿南直駐重兵，河南、山西、陝西各要隘並力堵截，速調駐熱河、綏遠之蒙古馬隊進口內衛京畿；

translations.literal: When Guangdong rebels invaded north, Xincun memorialized that rebel flames were drawing near, asking to hold the river line, station heavy forces directly south of the capital, block all key passes in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi together, and quickly move Mongol cavalry stationed at Rehe and Suiyuan into the interior to guard the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: As Taiping forces marched north he urged holding the river line, massing troops south of Beijing, blocking Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi passes, and bringing Mongol cavalry from Rehe and Suiyuan to guard the capital;

sentences.zh: 京師九門嚴緝姦宄，運通倉存糧入城；

translations.literal: strictly hunt traitors at the capital's nine gates and move grain from the Tongcang into the city;
translations.idiomatic: hunt traitors at the nine gates and move Tongcang grain into the city;

sentences.zh: 並敕琦善、鄧紹良規复揚州、鎮江，為會剿江寧之計。

translations.literal: and order Qi Shan and Deng Shaoliang to plan recovery of Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as a plan for joint suppression of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: and order Qi Shan and Deng Shaoliang to recover Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as prelude to retaking Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳順天防務，畫分汛地，舉行團練；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on Shuntian defenses, dividing garrison zones and organizing militia;
translations.idiomatic: He also divided Shuntian defense zones and organized militia;

sentences.zh: 府屬各營舊隸總督管轄，請旨暫歸調遣。

translations.literal: the various camps under the prefecture had formerly been under the governor-general's jurisdiction; he asked that for the present they be placed under his dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: and asked that camps formerly under the governor-general answer to him for the moment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊犯天津，僧格林沁率師進剿，命順天府設糧台。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Tianjin; Sengge Rinchen led troops to suppress them, and Shuntian was ordered to set up a grain bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels threatened Tianjin; Sengge Rinchen marched out and Shuntian set up a grain bureau.

sentences.zh: 心存請發內帑三十二萬兩、京倉米二千六百石以給軍食，添制軍需火藥。

translations.literal: Xincun asked to issue three hundred twenty thousand taels from the inner treasury and two thousand six hundred shi of capital-granary rice for army provisions, and to add manufacture of military gunpowder.
translations.idiomatic: Xincun secured 320,000 taels from the inner treasury and 2,600 shi of capital grain for the army, plus more gunpowder.

sentences.zh: 又偕團防大臣會議京城防守事宜，舉光祿寺卿宋晉、太僕寺卿王茂廕綜理其事，並詔允行。

translations.literal: He also met with the capital defense commissioners to discuss capital defense, recommending Court of Imperial Entertainments minister Song Jin and Court of the Imperial Stud minister Wang Maoyin to oversee the matter—all approved by edict.
translations.idiomatic: He met defense commissioners, put Song Jin and Wang Maoyin in charge of capital defense, and won approval.

sentences.zh: 時議行鈔幣，心存疏言：「軍營搭放票鈔，諸多窒礙。

translations.literal: At the time paper money was under discussion; Xincun memorialized: 'Issuing paper notes in army camps has many obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: When paper money was debated, he wrote: 'Paying troops in paper notes faces many obstacles.

sentences.zh: 鈔幣之法，施行當有次第，此時甫經頒發，並未試用，勢難驟用之軍營。」

translations.literal: The method of paper currency should be applied in due order; it has only just been issued and not yet tried—it will be hard to use it suddenly in army camps.'
translations.idiomatic: Currency reform needs stages; notes have just been issued and untested—they cannot be forced on the army yet.'

sentences.zh: 詔斥為阻撓，即責籌次等施行之法，俾無阻滯。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked this as obstruction and immediately charged him to devise graded methods of implementation so there would be no hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called this obstruction and ordered him to devise workable steps at once.

sentences.zh: 會言官論通州捕役勾結土匪行劫，命刑部侍郎文瑞鞫得實，心存以徇庇革職。

translations.literal: When censors discussed Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits to rob, Vice Minister of Justice Wen Rui investigated and found it true; Xincun was dismissed for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: When censors exposed Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits, Wen Rui proved it and Xincun was dismissed for shielding them.

sentences.zh: 四年，起授吏部侍郎，調戶部，擢兵部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, transferred to Revenue, promoted Minister of War, and transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he was recalled as vice minister of personnel, moved to revenue, made war minister, then personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏陳江南軍事，略曰：「蘇、松、常、太三府一州，及浙之杭、嘉、湖三府，久為賊所窺伺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized on Jiangnan military affairs, in part saying: 'The three prefectures and one department of Su, Song, Chang, and Tai, and the three prefectures of Hang, Jia, and Hu in Zhe, have long been eyed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he memorialized on Jiangnan military affairs, in part saying: "Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Taicang, and Zhejiang's Hang, Jia, and Hu had long been rebel targets.

sentences.zh: 今寧國先陷，逼近宜興，向榮近守丹陽，溧水、句容相繼失守，宜責向榮嚴扼丹陽，令張國樑率精兵駐宜興扼東壩，別簡水師駐太湖，庶蘇、常兩郡可保無事。

translations.literal: Now Ningguo has fallen first and draws near Yixing; Xiang Rong recently holds Danyang; Lishui and Jurong have fallen in succession. Xiang Rong should be charged strictly to hold Danyang; Zhang Guoliang should be ordered to lead picked troops to garrison Yixing and block Dongba; separately select naval forces to garrison Taihu—then the two prefectures Su and Chang may be kept secure.
translations.idiomatic: With Ningguo fallen near Yixing and Lishui and Jurong lost, he urged Xiang Rong to hold Danyang, Zhang Guoliang to block Dongba from Yixing, and a fleet on Taihu to save Suzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 又近有按畝捐輸，失政體，竭民財，請查明停止。」

translations.literal: Recently there has also been donation by the mu; this loses the proper form of government and exhausts the people's wealth—please investigate and stop it.'
translations.idiomatic: Recently there has also been per-mu donation—this loses proper form of government and exhausts the people's wealth; please investigate and stop it."

sentences.zh: 是年冬，兼翰林院掌院學士，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，尋調戶部。

translations.literal: That winter he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, as Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Secretary, and soon was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he also headed the Hanlin, became associate grand secretary while personnel minister, then moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he became chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍北犯，天津戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Anglo-French allies invaded north and Tianjin was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Anglo-French forces marched north and Tianjin went on alert.

sentences.zh: 心存疏請聖駕還宮，以定眾志，力言京師重地，不可駐外國領事；

translations.literal: Xincun memorialized asking the sacred carriage to return to the palace to settle popular will, strongly stating that the capital is a vital place and foreign consuls must not be stationed there;
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor back to Beijing to steady morale and insisted foreign consuls must not stay in the capital;

sentences.zh: 長江形勢不可失；

translations.literal: the Yangzi's strategic position must not be lost;
translations.idiomatic: the Yangzi must not be abandoned;

sentences.zh: 綏芬邊地不可捐；

translations.literal: the Suifen borderlands must not be ceded;
translations.idiomatic: Suifen territory must not be surrendered;

sentences.zh: 兵費不可再償；

translations.literal: war expenses must not be paid again;
translations.idiomatic: war indemnities must not be paid again;

sentences.zh: 傳教不可推廣；

translations.literal: missionary activity must not be expanded;
translations.idiomatic: missionary activity must not expand;

sentences.zh: 和議難成，宜速進剿。

translations.literal: peace talks will be hard to conclude—rapid advance and suppression should be made.
translations.idiomatic: peace would be hard—strike quickly instead.

sentences.zh: 湖北巡撫胡林翼奏除漕務中飽之弊，請改徵折色。

translations.literal: Hubei Governor Hu Linyi memorialized on removing the graft in tribute transport and asked to collect in cash instead.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei governor Hu Linyi asked to end tribute-grain graft by collecting in cash.

sentences.zh: 心存力贊其議；

translations.literal: Xincun strongly endorsed his proposal;
translations.idiomatic: Xincun strongly backed him;

sentences.zh: 由部定章程五事，滿、漢兵糧折價支給，上下衙門一切陋規概行裁革焉。

translations.literal: the ministry fixed five regulations; Manchu and Han military grain rations were paid at cash prices, and all corrupt practices in upper and lower offices were in general abolished.
translations.idiomatic: the ministry set five rules, paid troops in cash, and abolished corrupt practices throughout.

sentences.zh: 拜體仁閣大學士，管理戶部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall and managed the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand secretary of the Tiren Hall and headed revenue.

sentences.zh: 與肅順同官不相能，屢乞病，不許。

translations.literal: He could not get along with Sushun, who held the same office, and repeatedly begged leave on grounds of illness but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with colleague Sushun and repeatedly begged sick leave in vain.

sentences.zh: 九年，复固請，乃予告去職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again firmly requested it and was granted leave to quit office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he insisted again and was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 十年，戶部迭興大獄，肅順主之，多所羅織。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Ministry of Revenue repeatedly launched major cases, which Sushun directed and in which many were ensnared.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 revenue launched major prosecutions directed by Sushun that ensnared many.

sentences.zh: 怡親王載垣等會鞫，謂司員忠麟、王熙震以短號鈔兌換長號，曾面啟心存，心存回奏部院事非一二人所能專政，斷無立談數語改舊章之理。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Zaiyuan and others jointly tried the case, saying that department clerks Zhonglin and Wang Xizhen exchanged short-number notes for long-number notes and had reported this to Xincun in person; Xincun replied that ministry affairs were not something one or two men could monopolize, and there was certainly no changing old regulations in a few words of standing talk.
translations.idiomatic: At trial Prince Yi Zaiyuan's faction claimed clerks Zhonglin and Wang Xizhen swapped short for long banknotes after briefing Xincun; Xincun replied that revenue policy was not decided in a hallway chat.

sentences.zh: 載垣等遂請褫頂帶歸案訊質，文宗鑑其誣，僅以失察議處，免傳訊，議降五級，改俟補官，革職留任。

translations.literal: Zaiyuan and others then asked that his official hat tassel be removed and he be sent back for interrogation; Wenzong saw the slander and only censured him for lack of oversight, exempted him from summons for trial, reduced five ranks, changed to await reassignment, dismissed from office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded his arrest; Xianfeng saw the frame-up and only punished lax oversight—no interrogation, a five-rank demotion, then retention in post pending reassignment.

sentences.zh: 復以五「宇」商號添支經費，心存駁令議減，未陳奏，司員即列入奏銷，下嚴議，革職留任。

translations.literal: Again, five merchant houses with the character Yu added expenses; Xincun rejected and ordered discussion to reduce them, but before memorializing the clerks included them in the memorial for expenditure approval; severe censure followed, dismissed from office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: When five "Yu" firms padded expenses, Xincun ordered cuts but clerks slipped them into accounts before he could memorialize; he was severely censured and kept on in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，車駕將幸熱河，心存上疏切諫。

translations.literal: That autumn the imperial carriage was about to go to Rehe; Xincun memorialized urgently remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, as the court prepared to flee to Rehe, Xincun sent an urgent remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 十一年，文宗崩於行在，梓宮還京，心存偕諸臣迎謁，特詔起用，以大學士銜管理工部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Wenzong died at the traveling palace; when the coffin returned to the capital Xincun together with other ministers went to meet and attend; a special edict recalled him to service with the rank of Grand Secretary managing the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Xianfeng died at Rehe; Xincun met the returning coffin and was recalled as grand secretary heading works.

sentences.zh: 疏舉人材，詔嘉其不失以人事君之義。

translations.literal: He memorialized recommending talent; an edict praised that he had not failed in the duty of serving one's lord through men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended talent; the throne praised his loyalty in staffing the state.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「東南之民鄉義甚堅，各郡縣陷後，流亡渡江者，日夜思招練義勇，克復鄉里。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: 'The people of the southeast are very firm in local loyalty; after each prefecture and county fell, refugees who crossed the river day and night think of recruiting militia to recover their native places.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "The people of the southeast are fiercely loyal; after each prefecture and county fell, refugees crossing the Yangzi day and night dreamed of raising militia to retake their homes.

sentences.zh: 請敕曾國籓擇能辦賊者馳赴通州東台​​，收拾將散之人心，激勵方興之義旅，進搗蘇、常，退保下河。

translations.literal: We ask that Zeng Guofan be ordered to select men able to deal with bandits and hurry to Tongzhou and Dongtai, gather hearts about to scatter, encourage rising loyal forces, advance against Su and Chang, and fall back to guard the lower river region.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zeng Guofan send able commanders to Tongzhou and Dongtai to rally morale, spur loyal militia, advance on Suzhou and Changzhou, and hold the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 上海一隅賦稅所出，宜取江海關無窮之利，以供曾國籓有用之兵。」

translations.literal: The tax revenue of the Shanghai corner should draw the boundless profits of the Jianghai customs to supply Zeng Guofan's useful troops.'
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai's customs revenue should draw the boundless profits of the Jianghai customs to supply Zeng Guofan's useful troops."

sentences.zh: 疏上，被嘉納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，入直弘德殿，偕祁俊藻等授穆宗讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he entered regular duty at the Hongde Hall, together with Qi Junzao and others instructing Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he tutored Tongzhi in the Hongde Hall alongside Qi Junzao and others.

sentences.zh: 兩宮皇太后慎重師傅之選，倚畀彌篤。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers were careful in choosing tutors and relied on him ever more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers chose tutors carefully and relied on him ever more.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，寢疾，子安徽巡撫同書方緣事繫獄，詔暫釋侍疾。

translations.literal: That winter he took to bed with illness; his son Anhui Governor Tongshu was imprisoned over a case, and an edict temporarily released him to attend his father.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill that winter while his son Tongshu, Anhui governor, was in prison; Tongshu was briefly released to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，優詔賜卹，稱其「品端學粹，守正不阿」，贈太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: Soon he died; a gracious edict granted condolence, calling him 'upright in character and pure in learning, upright and unyielding,' posthumously granting Grand Guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; the throne mourned his 'upright character and pure learning,' made him grand guardian posthumously, enshrined him among worthies, and named him Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫曾源進士，曾榮舉人，曾純、曾桂並以原官即用，曾翰賜內閣中書。

translations.literal: His grandson Zengyuan was granted jinshi; Zengrong provincial graduate; Zengchun and Zenggui were all appointed at their former ranks; Zenghan was granted secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zengyuan received the jinshi degree; Zengrong the juren; Zengchun and Zenggui kept their ranks; Zenghan became a grand secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 逾年，文宗實錄告成，以心存曾充監修總裁，賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: The next year when Wenzong's Veritable Record was completed, because Xincun had served as chief supervising compiler, a sacrificial altar was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfeng's Veritable Record was finished the next year, he received a sacrificial altar for having directed it.

sentences.zh: 子同書、同龢自有傳，同爵官湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: His sons Tongshu and Tonghe have separate biographies; Tongjue was Hubei governor.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Tongshu and Tonghe have their own biographies; Tongjue was governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 彭蘊章，字詠莪，江蘇長洲人，尚書啟豐曾孫。

translations.literal: Peng Yunzhang, courtesy name Yong'e, was a man of Changzhou in Jiangsu, great-grandson of Minister Qifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yunzhang, courtesy name Yong'e, came from Changzhou in Jiangsu and was great-grandson of Minister Qifeng.

sentences.zh: 由舉人入貲為內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: From provincial graduate he purchased office as secretary in the Grand Secretariat and served as Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he bought office as a grand secretariat secretary and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，成進士，授工部主事，仍留直軍機處。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was appointed director in the Ministry of Works, and still remained on duty at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1835, was made a works director, and stayed on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，歷鴻臚寺少卿、光祿寺少卿、順天府丞、通政司副使、宗人府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, vice governor of Shuntian, vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, and vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through director, vice minister of sacrifices and of imperial entertainments, Shuntian vice governor, transmission vice commissioner, and imperial clan vice director.

sentences.zh: 督福建學政，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Fujian and was transferred vice censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised Fujian examinations and became left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，疏言：「漕船衛官需索旗丁日益增多，沿途委員及漕運衙門、倉場花戶皆有費，慾減旗丁幫費，宜探本窮源。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he memorialized: 'Grain-transport guard officials' exactions of banner boatmen grow daily; commissioners along the route and the grain transport yamen and granary brokers all take fees. To reduce banner boatmen's assistance fees, one should trace to the root.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he memorialized: "Grain-transport guard officials' exactions of banner boatmen grow daily; commissioners along the route and the grain transport yamen and granary brokers all take fees. To reduce banner boatmen's assistance fees, one must trace to the root.

sentences.zh: 又州縣辦漕，應令督撫察其潔己愛民者，每歲酌保一二員；

translations.literal: For prefectures and counties handling tribute grain, governors and governors-general should inspect those who keep themselves clean and love the people and each year recommend one or two;
translations.idiomatic: He urged governors to reward clean, humane county officials handling tribute grain each year;

sentences.zh: 辦理不善者，劾一二員。

translations.literal: for those who handle it badly, impeach one or two.
translations.idiomatic: and impeach the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 運漕官及坐糧廳如能潔己剔弊，準漕督、倉場保奏，不稱職者劾罷。」

translations.literal: Transport officials and the grain-assessment office, if they can keep themselves clean and remove abuses, may be recommended by the grain transport director and granary superintendent; those unfit for office should be impeached and dismissed.'
translations.idiomatic: Clean transport officials could be recommended by the grain transport director and granary superintendent; those unfit for office should be impeached and dismissed."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministries discussed and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎，仍留學政任。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of Works while still retaining the education commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of works while keeping the education post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，命在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was ordered to serve above the Grand Council ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was ordered to serve above the Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 四年，調禮部，尋擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Rites, and soon promoted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he moved to rites, then soon became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 五年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜文淵閣大學士，管理工部及戶部三庫事務，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall, managed Works and the three treasuries of Revenue, and was chief tutor of the Upper Study.
