translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he became Wenyuan grand secretary, headed works and revenue's three treasuries, and chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 八年，京師旱，糧價踴貴，旗民生計益艱，蘊章奏請撥款採米，允之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the capital suffered drought and grain prices soared; banner people's livelihood grew harder; Yunzhang memorialized asking to allocate funds to purchase rice, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 drought drove up Beijing grain prices; Yunzhang secured funds to buy rice for the banners.

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「自改用大錢，城中米貴，疊荷加恩賑濟，又加米折，然民生疾苦未見轉機。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: 'Since large cash was introduced, rice in the city is dear; though grace has repeatedly granted relief and rice allowances were added, the people's hardship has not yet turned.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized: "Since large cash was introduced, rice in the city has stayed dear; though grace has repeatedly granted relief and rice allowances were added, the people's hardship has not yet turned.

sentences.zh: 臣聞兵丁所領止有實米二成，其餘折色定價，每石京錢四千至三千不等，大米一石市價京錢三十千。

translations.literal: I hear soldiers receive only two-tenths in actual grain; the rest is paid at a fixed cash price, from four thousand to three thousand capital cash per shi, while a shi of rice in the market costs thirty thousand capital cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers received only twenty percent in grain; the rest was paid in cash at three to four thousand per shi while market rice cost thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 持此折價買米，不過升斗。

translations.literal: Using this cash price to buy rice yields only a sheng or a dou.
translations.idiomatic: That cash bought only a cup or two of rice.

sentences.zh: 民生之蹙，不獨在無銀，並在無米。

translations.literal: The people's distress lies not only in lack of silver but also in lack of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The poor suffered from lack of rice as much as lack of silver.

sentences.zh: 本年海運多於上年，可將兵米酌量加增。

translations.literal: This year's sea transport exceeds last year's; military grain allotments may appropriately be increased in measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport exceeded last year's; military grain rations could be raised.

sentences.zh: 又各營養育兵及鰥寡孤獨小口米不過四萬餘名，每名歲支一石六斗，擬請此項酌給米，毋庸折色。

translations.literal: Also in the various camps the rice for nurturing soldiers and for widows, orphans, and the solitary numbers a little more than forty thousand persons; each person receives 1.6 shi yearly—we propose that for this item rice be given in kind without cash conversion.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed giving rice in kind to some forty thousand dependents instead of cash.

sentences.zh: 自前年以來，有提存部庫採買銀，又存四川、山東、山西、河南、陝西解京米價銀，共有四十七萬餘兩，堪以採買米石，加放兵米。

translations.literal: Since the year before last there has been silver set aside in the ministry treasury for purchase, and also rice-price silver submitted from Sichuan, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, and Shaanxi, totaling more than 470,000 taels, which can purchase rice to supplement military grain distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Some 470,000 taels in treasury reserves could buy rice for troops.

sentences.zh: 又有河南停運節省運腳銀二萬兩，堪為轉運之用。

translations.literal: There is also 20,000 taels of transport savings from Henan's suspended shipments, usable for transshipment.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's saved transport funds of 20,000 taels could pay shipping.

sentences.zh: 伏乞飭部採買，以資搭放，實於旗兵生計大有裨益。」

translations.literal: We humbly pray that the ministry be ordered to purchase so as to supply distribution—it will greatly benefit banner soldiers' livelihood.'
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that the ministry be ordered to purchase so as to supply distribution—it will greatly benefit banner soldiers' livelihood."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the ministries discussed and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 蘊章久直樞廷，廉謹小心，每與會議，必持詳慎。

translations.literal: Yunzhang long served on the council, was incorrupt and careful; whenever he joined deliberations he always held to thorough caution.
translations.idiomatic: Long on the council, Yunzhang was honest and cautious in every deliberation.

sentences.zh: 鈔票、科場諸大獄，婉體調護，與肅順等意忤。

translations.literal: In major cases over paper notes and the examination halls he tactfully mediated and was at odds with Sushun and others.
translations.idiomatic: In note and examination scandals he softened blows and clashed with Sushun.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督何桂清素以才敏自負，蘊章誤信之，數於上前稱薦。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor-General He Guiqing had always prided himself on quick talent; Yunzhang mistakenly trusted him and repeatedly praised him before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing of Liangjiang was clever and self-confident; Yunzhang wrongly praised him repeatedly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十年，江寧大營潰，蘊章猶言桂清可恃。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the great camp at Jiangning collapsed, yet Yunzhang still said Guiqing could be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, after the Nanjing camp collapsed, Yunzhang still insisted He Guiqing could be trusted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蘇、常相繼陷，桂清逮治。

translations.literal: Before long Su and Chang fell in succession and Guiqing was arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Suzhou and Changzhou fell and He Guiqing was arrested.

sentences.zh: 文宗以蘊章無知人鑑，眷注浸衰。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because Yunzhang lacked judgment of men, gradually cooled in favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng lost confidence in Yunzhang's judgment of men.

sentences.zh: 適有足疾，扶掖入直，命毋庸在軍機大臣上行走，以示體恤。

translations.literal: Just then he had foot ailment and was helped in to duty; he was ordered no longer to serve above the Grand Council ministers, as a mark of consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Foot trouble made him lean on attendants; he was relieved of Grand Council duty as a kindness.

sentences.zh: 尋奏乞罷職，出都就醫。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized begging to leave office and left the capital for medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and left Beijing for treatment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿久任樞垣，備悉時事。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'You have long served on the council and are thoroughly familiar with current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "You know the times from long council service.

sentences.zh: 現在軍務如有見及，並採訪輿論民情，隨時具疏交地方官大吏代遞。」

translations.literal: If you have views on military affairs, and gather public opinion and popular sentiment, at any time submit a memorial through local high officials to forward.'
translations.idiomatic: If you have views on military affairs, gather public opinion and popular sentiment, and at any time submit a memorial through local high officials to forward."

sentences.zh: 蘊章密陳時務六則，報聞。

translations.literal: Yunzhang secretly memorialized six points on current affairs and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang sent six secret points on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，病痊，署兵部尚書，尋兼署左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when his illness healed, he acted as Minister of War, and soon also acted as Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, recovered, he acted as war minister and then left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，復以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he again begged to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he again begged retirement on illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，依大學士例賜卹，諡文敬。

translations.literal: Before long he died; condolence was granted according to the precedent for grand secretaries, posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died with grand-secretary funeral honors and the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子祖賢，官至湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: His son Zuxian rose to Hubei governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuxian became governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文宗初政，杜受田以師傅最被信任，贊畫獨多。

translations.literal: The commentators say: At the beginning of Wenzong's reign Du Shoutian, as tutor, was most trusted and alone contributed much to planning.
translations.idiomatic: The historians note: early in Xianfeng's reign Du Shoutian, as tutor, was most trusted and shaped policy most.

sentences.zh: 祈俊藻、彭蘊章皆久領樞務，翁心存數論軍事，久筦度支。

translations.literal: Qi Junzao and Peng Yunzhang both long led council affairs; Weng Xincun repeatedly discussed military affairs and long managed revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Junzao and Peng Yunzhang long led the council; Weng Xincun often debated war and long ran revenue.

sentences.zh: 三人者並與肅順不協，先後去位；

translations.literal: All three were at odds with Sushun and left office in turn;
translations.idiomatic: All three clashed with Sushun and left office;

sentences.zh: 同治初元，聯翩復起。

translations.literal: at the beginning of Tongzhi they returned to office in succession.
translations.idiomatic: at Tongzhi's start they returned in succession.

sentences.zh: 俊藻、心存三朝耆碩，輔導衝主，一時清望所歸焉。

translations.literal: Junzao and Xincun were venerable elders of three reigns who guided a young sovereign—the pure reputation of the age rallied to them.
translations.idiomatic: Junzao and Xincun were three-reign elders tutoring a child emperor—the age's moral authority gathered around them.
